lens: What must not be lost, and where the critique needs arguing (the tensions between Ren's own directions; what is strong; what a rewrite cannot fix; how fourteen AI-scored rounds produced a 4)
in_one_paragraph: Ren's judgment of the public face is right, and I can show it with counts. The "first screen" states 11–14 minutes, the "one page" 29–37. On the site home the first picture comes after about 2,400 px of prose. The "map" is eight boxes with counts between them. The "connection map" joins folders to chapter files, not things in the world. But the critique is incomplete in three ways. First, much of what he dislikes was built on his own earlier words: keep everything, label AI text, exact scope, "a time is a guide, pursue complete expression", and "keep going until everything is at least 8/10". A redesign has to reconcile those with the new critique, and the reconciliation is by layer: exactness, provenance and completeness each live once at a home, and entry pages are a strict selection with a hard word cap. Second, part of the difficulty is in the theory, not the prose. The atlas has no states as nodes: 251 of 321 exits end in a sentence, not a node. By the method chapter's own count, 11 of 117 central declarations derive from the root. The work's own review calls the central theorems near-definitional or known. The ethics was re-said about nine times in a month. 838 of the 1,183 crosswalk entries read the project's own earlier folders, and 327 of the 345 entries on outside traditions and sciences rest on AI recall. A fifteenth rewrite of the fronts fixes none of this. Third, the process that scored near 8 was a closed loop of the kind the theory itself describes: AI-written pages, a rubric written by the same sessions, AI readers with no attention limit who were told the purpose in advance and told not to mark length down. The strong material is real and buried: the capture chain with ten recorded joins (six proved), the four questions, the fishers test, the failures-first table of tests, the premise ledger, the known-results table, and the method chapter's paragraph that predicted this failure on 24 October. That should become the centre.

Reconciliation: "complete expression" applies to the page where a thing has its home (a chapter section, a record). An entry page's job is entry, so it gets a hard word cap that a test enforces, and any addition names what it displaces. Completeness is a property of the whole site, not of each page.

Two of his rules are in tension here: his words are kept verbatim, and the opening is revised on argument. proposals.change: Change what counts as done: a person's cold read closes a round; AI readers check facts and simulate a time-limited newcomer, and give no scores.
proposals.how: (1) A front is done when Ren, and then two or three people outside the work, read the home for five minutes on the site and say back in two sentences what it is and what they would open next, and the say-back matches the makers' intent. Record their words verbatim in sources/. (2) Between human reads the home and layer-1 leads are frozen; AI sessions may fix facts but not re-word. (3) AI cold readers get only the rendered page, no repository, no AGENTS.md, and a budget: the first 250 words, then three clicks. They return a say-back, the words they did not know, and where they stopped. No number. (4) A separate AI checker compares each front sentence with its home for drift and repairs at the home or by deleting from the front, never by adding a qualifier to the front. (5) A word-cap test replaces the score threshold. (6) Each round reports what was removed.
proposals.what_it_risks_or_loses: It is slow and depends on people's time. The run-hold already waits on 'the first people who read it', and I found no report recorded. Ren's own say-back is not a newcomer's, since he knows the vocabulary, so outsiders are needed. Simulated cold readers are still AI and share the writers' blind spots; they are a filter before the human read, not a substitute.

where_ren_may_be_wrong_or_incomplete:
1. "Another round" will not do it. If the critique is read as a presentation problem, the next step is a fifteenth rewrite. Part of what makes the pages hard is that the theory has no small centre yet: no states as nodes, 11 of 117 central declarations derived from the root, an ethics still moving, and a wisdom map that is mostly the project's own folders. The fronts are long partly because the prose is doing the joining that the theory has not done.

2. A graph of the topology cannot be drawn honestly today beyond about ten nodes. A handsome global map would say more than is there. The right first picture is small (the capture chain), with the unplaced remainder counted.

3. Wikipedia works because each article is about one thing that can be defined in ordinary words in its first sentence. A wiki of the 183 theorem-named dynamics would be the atlas again. The unit has to be places, concepts and cases. A wiki also carries no argument, so one linear page is still needed.

4. Confidence is the wrong target if it is aimed at directly. A face tuned so that a reader feels confident is a selection on what the reader reads, and the work's own law says what that drains. Confidence should come from one thing a reader can check in ten minutes: the fishers test, the four questions on their own system, or the failures page.

5. "Don't mention AI so much" must not remove the mark from the 327 readings of traditions made from AI recall, nor from the literature review that found the theorems known. Those are the places where the label carries information.
